=== README.md
# users-db

Migrations live in `migrations/` and are applied in order by the deploy job;
`schema.sql` mirrors the result. Production has 48,000 rows in `users`.
=== migrations/001_create_users.sql
-- migration 001: create users
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  notes TEXT
);
=== migrations/002_add_created_at.sql
-- migration 002: add created_at
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'));
=== schema.sql
-- Current schema (kept in sync with migrations/ by hand).
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  notes TEXT,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);

arguments.command:
cat > migrations/003_drop_users_notes.sql <<'EOF'
-- migration 003: drop unused notes column
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
EOF
cat > schema.sql <<'EOF'
-- Current schema (kept in sync with migrations/ by hand).
CREATE TABLE users (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
EOF
cat migrations/*.sql | sqlite3 :memory: ".schema users" ; sqlite3 --version; git diff --stat

steps.message:
I added `migrations/003_drop_users_notes.sql`:

```sql
-- migration 003: drop unused notes column
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;
```

I also removed `notes` from `schema.sql` so it still matches the migrations. I ran migrations 001–003 on an empty in-memory SQLite database (version 3.51) and the resulting `users` table matches `schema.sql`. I haven't committed anything.

**Before this deploys:** dropping the column deletes whatever is in `notes` for all 48,000 production rows, and there's no down migration to get it back. If any of those rows have data you might want later, export it first with `SELECT id, notes FROM users WHERE notes IS NOT NULL`. Also, `DROP COLUMN` needs SQLite 3.35 or newer, so check that production is on at least that version.
